subject: FluxAI onboarding — performance & unit-cost kickoff
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya@flux.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Vega <carlos@flux.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Kickoff: FluxAI onboarding (perf focus)

Hi Alex / Laura,

Thanks for the quick responses this week. We'd like to kick off the technical onboarding next week and make sure the first sprint prioritizes unit-cost improvements without degrading latency for our interactive assistants. Top concerns on our side: token cost, tail latency >300ms for the 95th percentile, and making a safe fallback plan for peak traffic.

Can Redwood come prepared to discuss: batching vs per-request latency tradeoffs, prefix/KV caching strategies for repeated conversational context, recommended quantization profiles for our model family (Eleuther-like 33B variant), and routing policies (priority by region + cost-tier fallback)?

I've attached a short token distribution sample and our current traffic profile. Proposed kickoff slot: Thu Apr 6 10:00am PT — does that work?

Thanks,
Maya Singh
Lead ML Engineer
FluxAI

Subject: Re: Kickoff: FluxAI onboarding (perf focus)

Maya — appreciate the context and the sample traffic. Thu Apr 6 10:00am PT works on our side; calendar invite sent.

Agenda (30–45m):
- Introductions & success criteria (5m)
- Traffic profile review & target SLOs for latency/cost (5m)
- Quick wins: KV/prefix caching strategy and recommended cache keys (5m)
- Batching strategy: latency budgets vs throughput (10m)
- Quantization matrix & safety/quality checks (10m)
- Routing & fallback plan: model variants + regional routing (5m)

Pre-kickoff deliverables (we'll bring these as attachments in the invite):
- A short onboarding agenda PDF with concrete tasks (flux_onboard_agenda.pdf)
- Quantization profile matrix tailored to your model family (quant_profile_matrix.xlsx)
- Implementation checklist with owner assignments

Quick notes for the meeting so we don't waste time:
- Laura will own the caching proposal and integration tasks (Laura will propose specific cache keys for session vs prompt-level reuse).
- Neha (implementation lead) will propose autoscale/batching thresholds and a canary plan for rolling quantized weights.
- Marissa (CS) will draft the mutual action plan and post-meeting deliverables.

Two specific asks for you before the call:
1) Are there any hard constraints on max acceptable latency for interactive flows (P95/P99 targets)?
2) Do you have a representative prompt set we can run the quantization safety checks on (preferably labeled pass/fail examples)?

We'll aim to present a cost vs quality tradeoff matrix during the call so you can pick the quantization profile that meets your quality bar.

See you Thu — attaching the short agenda and quant matrix preview.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 4 Apr 2028 12:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: FluxAI onboarding (perf focus)

Following up with a few specifics I'll present on Thu:

Caching proposal (high level)
- Session-level KV caching for conversational history truncated to last 2 prompts + assistant reply for high-reuse flows. Cache keys: user_id + conv_id + last_n_hash. TTL: 30m by default; evict on prompt schema change.
- Prompt prefix caching: store compiled prompt embeddings/partial KV states for templated system prompts. This gives big wins on token generation for assistants with repeated system directives.

Batching heuristics
- For sub-200ms latency budgets, prefer small micro-batches (batch_size 1–4) with an adaptive hold window (5–20ms) tuned by observed QPS.
- For throughput-oriented endpoints (background reranking), use larger batch sizes with async worker pools and a separate endpoint.

Quantization safety notes
- We'll propose three profiles: Q8 (safe), Q6 (balanced), Q4 (aggressive, quality regression likely on long-context completion). We'll bring objective eval snapshots on a labeled prompt set.

Routing policy suggestion
- Primary routing by region + model variant. During congestion, fall back to a lower-cost quantized variant with a gradual degradation window and automatic rollback if eval regression exceeds threshold.

I'll include short CLI snippets and config samples in the follow-up doc so Neha can start carving the implementation tasks.

- Laura
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Maya Singh <maya@flux.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Carlos Vega <carlos@flux.ai>

Subject: Re: Kickoff: FluxAI onboarding (perf focus)

Thanks — the agenda looks great and the proposed owners make sense. A couple clarifications ahead of Thu:

- P95 target: 220ms for user-facing assistant endpoints. P99 ideally < 500ms but we can accept a small percentage of longer tails during heavy load.
- We attached a 500-item prompt set with pass/fail labels to the Drive folder — please use that for the quantization safety checks.
- Carlos asked whether Redwood can pre-run the Q6 profile on a 1000-request sample and share a short report before the call (latency distribution, token cost delta, top-5 regression examples). If you can run that, it would help us make a quicker decision in the meeting.

We'll plan to accept the mutual action plan during the call and assign internal owners from our side (I will own the validation step).

See you Thu,
Maya
